title_how: HubCo: buy carrier hubs, lease back, sell the rest

flow.detail: Acquire oversized central offices, MSCs, landing and C-RAN hubs with power, fiber and city-center permits
Seller signs a 15-year anchor lease for only the space and power its network still needs
Convert empty halls into neutral colocation, meet-me rooms and 0.5-2 MW edge/AI inference pods
Lease racks, power and cross-connects to other carriers, ISPs, CDNs, cloud and AI tenants

payers.pays_for: 15-year lease on space and power it keeps, with annual escalators
Racks, power and cross-connects to reach the anchor's network and each other
Edge colocation close to end users, plus interconnection ports
High-density power and cooling pods for low-latency inference in city centers

title_market: Stranded carrier real estate meets edge demand

title_plan: Proven deal type, phased entry from SBA markets

precedents.name: AT&T - Reign Capital (2025)
precedents.what: 74 central offices, 13M sq ft, US$850M+ upfront; AT&T leases back only needed space and shares in redevelopment upside

precedents.name: BT - Telereal (2001)
precedents.what: ~6,700 properties incl. ~6,000 exchanges for GBP 2.38B; 30-year leaseback at ~7.9% initial yield with 3% annual uplift

precedents.name: Telefonica legacy-to-edge (2026)
precedents.what: Converting copper central offices into 1-2 MW mini data centers: 10 live, 17 in 2026, target 100+ within 5-7 years

plan.milestones: Bid for 10-20 hubs from one LatAm carrier (e.g., Brazil or Central America) with 15-year leaseback; set up neutral meet-me rooms
Retrofit 1-2 MW per site; sign 3+ non-anchor tenants per hub; bundle with SBA towers and fiber for regional ISPs
Programmatic portfolio deals with 2-3 carriers incl. US copper retirements; JV capital to fund US$1B+ of hubs
